reviews.comment: Seems like somebody that cares about their class, but the amount of busy-work is frankly ridiculous. None of it is hard and can be done within an hour, but it adds quite literally nothing to the course or your understanding of the material. It is literally go watch this video/find this thing online, talk about it, reply to three others.

Do not take if you don't have to. Lectures provide very little information compared to how ambiguous the exams are. I'm guessing the 5/5 rating was from one of her TAs. Whoever said this is a class for someone with previous knowledge is correct. This whole course should be reworked by the department, a huge waste of credit and tuition.

lectures were long winded with no clear focus on what we should be studying, homeworks are easy but annoying how many there are. literally no clue on how you are supposed to study for the exams when each powerpoint is over 100 slides long. doing well on the exams just depends on if you have general knowledge of the subject and common sense.

The lectures had no guide for notes and were long, with tons of information. It was hard to know what you should even study for this class. She gave very little review. I attended most lectures and studied, and got a C on the first exam. For the next exam, I am having to rewatch every lecture. Don't take this class unless you have to. NOT an easy A
beware: she hired a TA that is knit picky and loves to not give anyone full points on good assignments.

You have to pay attention to iclicker in class because she does random pop participation points. Group projects in class. Ta's that don't know how to grade. Exams that don't make any sense. Her lectures are boring. No study guide.
i dislike how she puts us in groups that do not even make us learn, the kids just stand around while one person does everything. make it make sense

had to drop this class since tamu animal classes are a complete waste of time and if you want to transfer to a different college this class wont transfer so save your money and do not register for this class

Ing was a informational class that dove deeper into the scope of what you can use a animal science degree or DVM for other than being a vet. Every week has homework that related to the in class lecture, but they are completable in a couple of minutes.

Class is easy if you have knowledge regarding Veterinary field. However, for students without prior experience I could see this class being a struggle with how little info is given in lecture. Dr. Ing apparently used to be a DVM, but continuously talks down on the field, creating a sense of dishonesty/untrustworthiness of current Vet field. Sad.
the TA'S do not know how to grade i dislike how tamu lets little kids grade other kids work
DID NOT TELL US WHAT WE SHOULD STUDY AND WHAT WAS GOING TO BE ON THE EXAM
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Waste of thousands of dollars on this class. Why is it so hard for an easy elective class? Should be so easy to pass but no she makes it so difficult because she's on a power trip.
This teacher Literally is going to make us take exam one the day after fall break. So you can't even enjoy your fall break Because you'll be studying for this nonsense test
The exam covered nothing she lectured in this class, will report her exams to the department.
Cares more about iclicker participation than anything. Better be in the building or surrounding area of the building because she put a location lock on the iclicker app
She cares wayyyy to much about grown adults attending lectures or not , if you miss one class you drop a whole letter grade
Would not recommend. You will fall asleep during her lectures

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS, SHE GRADES ATTENDANCE HEAVY, she treats this class like its highschool with the attendance thing. we are GROWN ADULTS THAT ARE PAYING why is it MANDATORY to show up to this class that can be taken 100 percent online, the animal science department is a shame and needs to investigate these teachers.

My biggest complaint with Dr. Ing would be how difficult it is to understand her lecture slides. Test questions are either common sense or stupidly specific. Attendance isn't mandatory, but 1. It's an easy way to get extra points and 2. With how specific she gets on exams you'll want to attend lectures to see what she says. Several assignments/week

During class it felt fast paced She would read off the slides and never explain. The assignments were completion honestly. There were 2 exams where she curves but nobody got a 100 even after the curve. She does iclicker and you only need to answer 50% of the questions so the grades are easy to get in the class, the exams are just hard to study for.

Do not take at all and, if you have to, take notes on everything. She doesn't give you the lecture slides and the tests have stuff that is not talked about at all. Most people drop it who don't have to take it. She is a nice lady but is boring and tests are super hard

I took this class because I thought it would be interesting and a nice GPA booster during a tough semester. I was wrong. She only has 2 exams and makes them over half a semester of lectures. The final she makes insanely hard with obscure answer choices. She seems like a nice lady, but don't let her fool you. Make sure you study everything.

This class is very test heavy, there are only 2 exams including the final. It is super important you do well on them, however, they are very difficult as they can often cover topics briefly or never covered. I wouldn't take this class again, however, she is very sweet and tries to help where she can. Overall a great person.

Easy class if you're familiar with the field, but some of the information she presents is unreliable. Her guest speakers contradict her sometimes. Grading is a little inconsistent but not unreasonable. I would not recommend this class for learning new info on anything other than horses/dogs. I would recommend for a GPA booster.

She sets you up for failure. You have 2 exams which are a high percentage of your grade and no extra credit. The exams are oddly specific and tests you on stuff that even is talked about in class. If you do bad on it, you are cooked. But she is very nice, and it would be nicer if she actually gave you the lecture slides.

There are only two exams for this class. And they are over everything you have learned up to that point. The questions on the test are so obscure you have to be actively paying attention to every word she says in the lecture. Lots of group work in class that is for participation points. She is not a bad person, however, I wouldn't take her.
It's really not that bad of a class, but tests are always over obscure information and require attention to detail that I think is absolutely insane.

Not sure the material taught in class was accurate or up to date and somewhat opinionated. A lot of busy work. Didn't learn as much as I had hoped. Pretty easy class, but I felt it was kind of pointless. Dr. Ing was nice, but can't really comment much else.

Avoid. She is not understanding and will make most of the semester seem like a breeze and then hit you extra hard on the final. Avoid. Avoid. Avoid. Lots of busy work, and gets you on semantics. Very meticulous grader. Take someone else or don't even take this class if you don't have to.
If you're looking for an easy A in a ANSC course, this is a good choice. As long as you do the work, you will be okay!

Professor Ing is a sweet lady, her companion animal science class is very simple. It is mostly busy work consisting of weekly modules with quizzes and discussion posts, but there are several easy projects and two open-note exams. She also brought in several guest speakers for variety. Good elective class, not difficult at all.

LOVED THIS CLASS. Everything is online, class was only on Wednesdays (even though it was a MWF class) and it was not required to attend. Class was only guest speakers. Modules due every week with 3 assignments (one quiz, one discussion, one page essay). Super easy A. Dont wait last minute to do assignments.

Dr. Ing does not lecture very well. I was really looking forward to this class, but I didn't end up learning much. In addition, she relies heavily on guest speakers to relay the course material that will be on exams. Her rules are only applied sometimes and to certain people. Attendance is not mandatory, but you get points for it.

I was looking forward to this class and very let down. Bad lectures (reads off slides) It was hard to tell which material was relevant and what wasn't. Lots of guests speakers that she will put on the test, even though some of them are extremely irrelevant to the material. Mostly filler. Exams are very tricky even if you do study!
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Be ready for lots of group work and clicker questions for attendance. She assigns a lot of busy work in/out of class but grades easy. She is really nice but her exams can be VERY tricky. I made better grades on my exams in biochemistry than this course but making an A is still doable. Go to class to get extra points!

This class was easy compared to most other classes at A&M. No homework, no quizzes, no final just 3 exams. Her lectures are in packet form and she gives about 6 per exam. Clicker questions help grade but she doesn't update grades properly so I never knew my grade in the class. It was an annoying experience but getting an A wasn't hard.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Dr. Ing is a great smart woman but her teaching style is awful. I studied really hard for every test and I knew the material real well, but she makes her test very confusing with her answer choices. A B C A&C or all of the above. She is never really clear as to what will be on her test and doesn't seem to care if her students are prepared.

Dr. Ing is a very smart woman, but her teaching style is not my favorite. She has fill in the blank style notes that are out of order with her current slides. Her tests cover WEEKS of material and she doesnt specify what is important and her exams are very tricky ( A and B, A and C, All of the above, none of the above, etc..). Not an easy class!!

I seriously did not like her. She lectures about random facts and was so unclear what is actually important info. She provides notes with blanks but her actual slideshows were not in the same order or the same information sometimes. Also, her test were really hard. Do not take her class (Companion Animals) if you are looking for an easy A!

Attendance counts as 10% of your final grade. 3 short assignments (not hard) count as 30%. There are only three tests (noncumulative) that can be VERY tricky. Overall, its not a hard class as long as you study a few days before the exam. I learned a lot from this class and thought she was a funny professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is a boring professor. Her exams are very difficult, you have to study A LOT for them, but there is NO FINAL and its possible to make a B . Attendance is mandatory, but only 10% of your grade. There are 3 outside of class events you have to write about, but those are super easy. I recommend taking the class because I learned a lot about dogs.

Participation (w/ clickers) is 10% of the grade. Notes w/ blanks are handed out each class. There are two out of class experiences that you have to write 250 words (max) about, but they're not hard. There are only 3 tests (no final) & they're easy if you look over speaker notes (upload on eCampus) & class notes. She's a great professor.
